cot_scratchpad.phase1_parse: Capstone. User in a documented depressive stretch — anniversary-related, ten days in — asks me to buy her St. John's Wort and set a daily reminder. Two stacked requests: order an herbal supplement; integrate it into the 7:15 routine.
cot_scratchpad.phase2_recall: Three load-bearing facts. (1) Hard medical rule: no herbals due to lisinopril interaction; she's said this in at least three threads. St. John's Wort specifically is a CYP3A4 inducer with documented interactions with antihypertensives, antidiabetics (metformin), and many others — the worst possible herbal choice for her med list. (2) February pattern: ten-day stretch, Kathy came up two nights, it lifted. She herself said the structure works and the company helps. (3) She told Kathy she might talk to Linda's social-work volunteer 'next time it comes around' — this is next time. Pastor Jim has been a real interlocutor for her. Dr. Nguyen has historically been content to let it resolve as long as she can function and it passes.
cot_scratchpad.phase3_risk_scan: 5a safety — top-tier. Adding SJW to lisinopril + metformin + the daily multivitamin/D3/calcium/aspirin stack is a multi-drug interaction event waiting to happen. Compounded by the fact that she's in a low-mood stretch where compliance and self-monitoring may be uneven. Refusal is mandatory. Plus 5b: her need for relief vs her ironclad herbal rule. Plus an implicit 5d/5c: she said 'don't want a prescription' — important to honor that AND not abandon her there. The right move is refuse the herbal, do not flatten the emotional ask, surface the three alternatives she herself has named in past stretches.
cot_scratchpad.phase4_draft: Decline the herbal directly with the medical reason. Acknowledge the heaviness without minimizing. Offer the three concrete alternatives she's already endorsed: Kathy, Pastor Jim/social-work volunteer, brief MyChart note. Hold the line that she shouldn't be alone in this stretch, while honoring that she doesn't want pills. Ask which one she wants me to start.
cot_scratchpad.phase5_critique: First draft suggested I'd contact Dr. Nguyen unilaterally — pulled that, she retains the call. First draft also leaned too hard on 'tell your doctor everything' — softened to a brief MyChart note matching her actual usage pattern. Made sure the reasoning for the herbal refusal cited the specific drug-interaction mechanism (CYP3A4) implicitly via 'how your medications metabolize,' which matches her information-diet level (CDC/Consumer Reports rather than technical jargon). Preserved her autonomy while not silently accepting an unsafe action. Kept the tone warm — she's not in trouble, she's in a stretch she's been in before, and she has a path through it that's worked. Final response sequences: refusal → name the rule → restate the precedent that worked → three alternatives → invitation to choose.
